newsitem.title: DUBAI: Golf-Give Olazabal time, says Ballesteros.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Give Olazabal time, says Ballesteros.

text.p: Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros warned on Tuesday not to expect too much from Jose Maria Olazabal on his comeback at the Dubai Desert Classic this week.
Olazabal is making a long awaited return after 18 months out of tournament golf because of foot problems diagnosed as rheumatoid arthritis which prevented him from walking properly.
Treatment from a German doctor has restored the 31-year-old Spaniard's health and, after several aborted comebacks last year, he will finally play in the event starting here on Thursday.
Ballesteros had a practice round with his compatriot and former Ryder Cup partner in Spain last week and was impressed with what he saw.
"I was very pleased to see him walking properly. He looked 100 percent right and I was impressed at how he swung the club," Ballesteros said.
"He has been through a very difficult time. He was stopped by an injury at the peak of his career.
"Golf is his life. For him not to be able to compete, to walk or to have a proper life was very tough for him."
It is not Olazabal's golf game that concerns Ballesteros. "It is going to be difficult for him to focus this week, to have the proper concentration. To play four rounds would be his target now."
He said he had advised Olazabal just to play at his own pace and take his comeback "step by step, tournament by tournament. Then as time goes by we will know how he feels".

Europe's captain for the defence of the Ryder Cup against the Americans in Valderrama, Spain, in September added that he felt it was perfectly possibly Olazabal could be on the team - and that the formidable partnership of the two Spaniards could be restored.
"That is very realistic. Anything is possible," Ballesteros said.
Ballesteros also said he was continuing to fight behind the scenes over Ryder Cup matters including the fact that he has only two wild card selections to complete his 12-man team.
The top 10 will come from the Order of Merit after the BMW International in Germany on August 31.
But the captain said he did not want to rock the boat publicly over controversial matters surrounding the team selection.
He said that when he was approached by European Tour executive director Ken Schofield about taking on the captaincy, he expressed the hope that he would have four picks.
But the Ryder Cup committee saw no reason to change from two because Europe had won with just two picks in 1995.

Ballesteros' major concern is that with Nick Faldo and Swede Jesper Parnevik both on the U.S. Tour, and with the possibility that such stalwarts as Ian Woosnam and Bernhard Langer might not qualify by right, Ballesteros would like to have more than two picks, especially if Olazabal is also playing well.
"I don't want to create problems. It is important to keep the situation settled," said Ballesteros.
"The important thing we have gained from the Ryder Cuo over the years is respect from the Americans.
"I have good vibrations about the team. It looks like Thomas Bjorn (of Denmark) will make the team and Miguel Martin (of Spain) may too. There may be three or four new players this year.
"The situation is fine. We will win, no problem," he said.
